description: The operational dashboard for one InferOps release, as data: the questions an operator asks in the first thirty seconds, the panel that answers each, the PromQL every panel runs, and what the panel shows when there is no number to show. Every expression is held to the correlation query policy in tools/telemetry_correlation and evaluated against the committed synthetic scenarios. The Grafana dashboard JSON under deploy/grafana/ is generated from this file and compared against it. No Grafana has imported it and no Prometheus has evaluated a panel from it.

panels.title: Is this release's collector reaching anything, before any number below is read?

panels.description: The fraction of each tier's discovered targets that answered the last scrape. It says the collector reached a process, and nothing about whether that process can serve: a deleted pod has been observed reading up for fifteen seconds after deletion.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no target was discovered for any tier, or no collector is evaluating this release's recording rules. Every other panel is missing too until this one reads.

panels.title: Scrape targets answering, by tier

panels.description: A job whose selector matched no pod publishes no up series at all, so it is invisible in the panel beside this one. These read 1 in exactly that case.

defaults.noValue: No absence recorded: each job this profile renders has at least one target.

panels.title: Scrape jobs that discovered no pod

panels.description: Reads 1 whenever no API process in this release's namespace publishes inferops_build_info. That is a target answering without one, but it is also every API target down and a job that discovered nothing, because the recorded absence does not read up: read it beside the two scrape panels. The accepted query this repeats is named for the first case only, and that name says more than the expression does. While it reads 1, the since-start counts show missing rather than zero.

defaults.noValue: No absence recorded: an API process in this release published its identity.

panels.title: API identity not published
Is the API, the serving runtime, and the model ready?

panels.description: The API's own readiness refusals, counted since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas: the only readiness signal the platform emits. A count rather than a rate, because a rate cannot see the first refusal of a new component -- the recovery run's single refusal would have read 0 per second. A restarted process starts its count again.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.

panels.title: Readiness checks failed since the API processes started

panels.description: Which readiness component the API names when it refuses traffic: api or serving-adapter. inferops_component is not k8s_component, which is the workload tier. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears already at 1, so a rate never sees that first event, and a series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no readiness check has failed since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Readiness checks failed, by component

panels.description: inferops_model_ready is specified, assigned to the serving-runtime adapter, and emitted by nothing. The recorded absence reads 1 to say so rather than leaving an empty panel that reads as a ready model.

defaults.noValue: Not emitted: the serving-runtime adapter that owns inferops_model_ready is not instrumented, and no collector is evaluating the recorded absence either.

panels.title: Model readiness (not emitted)

panels.description: The kubelet sees the probes the chart renders, and the result reaches no series. llama-server's health endpoint is a probe target, not a metric. Scrape reachability, in the first row, is a different question.

options.content:
**Not answerable from current telemetry.**

The kubelet sees the probes the chart renders, and the result reaches no series. llama-server's health endpoint is a probe target, not a metric. Scrape reachability, in the first row, is a different question.

Would require: kube-state-metrics for pod phase and container readiness, and an instrumented serving-runtime adapter for runtime readiness.

panels.title: Pod, container, and runtime readiness (not answerable)
What traffic and concurrency are observable?

panels.description: Every request the API finished, every outcome, since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas. A count rather than a rate, so the first request of a process is counted; the per-second view is the timeseries beside it.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.

panels.title: Requests finished since the API processes started

panels.description: Outcome is one of success, client-error, server-error, and timeout. Summed across replicas on purpose: the question is about a workload, not a pod. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears already at 1, so a rate never sees that first event, and a series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no request has been finished since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Requests per second, by workload, model, and outcome

panels.description: Requests each API replica has accepted and not yet answered. instance is the pod name and the one unbounded label this dashboard shows; this panel is what it is paid for.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API replica has had a request since it started, or no API target is scraped. The in-flight series is created by a replica's first request; after that a replica with nothing in flight reads 0 and is present.

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_namespace, k8s_component, instance, inferops_workload_id, inferops_model_id) (inferops_inference_requests_in_flight)

panels.title: Requests in flight at the API, per replica

panels.description: The runtime's own view, through the chart's recording rules. It counts slots, not the API's accepted requests, and is not expected to match the API panel. Deferred says queueing happened and never how long anything waited.

defaults.noValue: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.

panels.title: Serving runtime: requests processing and deferred
What P50, P95, P99, and throughput can be derived from emitted metrics?

panels.description: Quantiles of inferops_inference_request_duration_seconds, with bucket counters summed across replicas before the quantile is taken. A quantile is interpolated inside a bucket, so its resolution is the catalog's bucket boundaries. An operating figure, not a benchmark. Once the bucket series exist, a five-minute window with no request makes every quantile NaN, which draws as a gap in a line that is still present -- not as this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no request has been finished since the API process started, so no bucket series exists, or no API target is scraped. An idle window after that shows gaps instead.

panels.title: Request duration P50, P95, and P99

panels.description: Request throughput: requests that finished with outcome success. Token throughput is in the token row. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears already at 1, so a rate never sees that first event, and a series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no request has succeeded since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The requests count separates the two.

panels.title: Successful requests per second, by model

panels.description: How long a request waits before the runtime starts on it. The deferred count in the traffic row is the partial substitute: it shows that queueing happened and never for how long.

defaults.noValue: Not emitted: inferops_inference_queue_duration_seconds is the serving-runtime adapter's measurement, and the adapter is not instrumented.

panels.title: Queue wait P95 (not emitted)
What errors are observable?

panels.description: Every canonical error the API counted since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas. A count rather than a rate, so a first error is never read as none.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.

panels.title: Errors counted since the API processes started

panels.description: Requests with an outcome other than success, over all requests, counted since each publishing API process started. Cumulative for the same reason as the counts: a rate would miss the first failure of a new outcome.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no request has been finished since the API processes started, and a share of no traffic is undefined rather than zero, or no API target is scraped. The requests count shows which.

panels.title: Share of requests that did not succeed, since the API processes started

panels.description: inferops_error_code is the platform's canonical code, never an HTTP status and never a provider's message; the collector drops an HTTP status label on the way in. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears already at 1, so a rate never sees that first event, and a series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no error has been counted since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Errors per second, by workload and canonical code
What model-load and recovery signals are emitted?

panels.description: The load durations this project has are stopwatch figures in evidence records, not series.

defaults.noValue: Not emitted: inferops_model_load_duration_seconds is assigned to the serving-runtime adapter, which is not instrumented, and llama-server publishes no load duration either.

panels.title: Model load duration P95 (not emitted)

panels.description: The recovery signal the API tier emits: a lost pod's identity series stops being returned once its target is marked stale, and its replacement publishes a new one under a new instance in the identity table. It counts processes the collector has read, not desired replicas, and it can lag a deletion by the discovery and scrape interval.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API process published an identity. This is not a zero.

panels.title: API processes publishing an identity

panels.description: The recovery run asked for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and received no series. A restart is visible here only indirectly, as an identity replaced under a new instance.

options.content:
**Not answerable from current telemetry.**

The recovery run asked for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and received no series. A restart is visible here only indirectly, as an identity replaced under a new instance.

Would require: kube-state-metrics.

panels.title: Restarts and pod phase (not answerable)
What CPU, memory, and replica state exist?

panels.description: CPU seconds per second from the API process's own counter. It is the process, not the container: a cgroup limit, throttling, and working set are all elsewhere and none has a source.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API target is scraped.

panels.title: API process CPU, per replica

panels.description: The catalog declares inferops_process_resident_memory_bytes, assigns it to the API, and marks it not emitted.

defaults.noValue: Not emitted: the only per-process memory figure the standard library exposes is a file, and a module under src/inferops may not read one.

panels.title: API process memory (not emitted)

panels.description: Neither the serving runtime's consumption nor any container's use against its declared request and limit reaches a series in the accepted cluster.

options.content:
**Not answerable from current telemetry.**

Neither the serving runtime's consumption nor any container's use against its declared request and limit reaches a series in the accepted cluster.

Would require: a kubelet cAdvisor scrape job, metrics-server, or kube-state-metrics, each a cluster add-on this chart does not own.

panels.title: Container and pod CPU and memory (not answerable)

panels.description: Pods with a metrics port the collector found in each tier. The nearest thing to a replica count this telemetry has, and not the same thing: it is neither the desired count nor the ready count, and during a replacement it has been observed to include the pod being removed.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no collector is evaluating this release's recording rules, or neither job has ever discovered a pod.

panels.title: Scrape targets discovered, by tier
Which model, runtime, workload, environment, and provider is running?

panels.description: One row per API process: service version, capability, release, environment, adapter kind, model and revision, runtime and image digest. inferops_adapter_kind reads mock or real, so a mock result stays visibly a mock. The chart's default leaves service_version empty, and an empty label value is shown as absent.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no API process published an identity. The collection row says whether a target answered without one.

panels.title: Build, model, and runtime identity, per API replica

panels.description: The environment, workload, model, and runtime the collector attaches to the runtime's series, and how many runtime processes carry them. The immutable identity -- revision, image digest -- is not reachable from a runtime series, because a runtime series cannot be joined to the API's identity series.

defaults.noValue: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.

panels.title: Serving runtime operating identity

panels.description: No telemetry attribute names the Kubernetes provider a release runs on. The provider is recorded in each evidence record, where the run that produced it was verified, and nowhere in a series.

options.content:
**Not answerable from current telemetry.**

No telemetry attribute names the Kubernetes provider a release runs on. The provider is recorded in each evidence record, where the run that produced it was verified, and nowhere in a series.

Would require: a provider attribute in the telemetry catalog with a permitted metric or identity placement, and an emitter that sets it from the verified target rather than from configuration.

panels.title: Cluster provider (not answerable)
What token data is available?

panels.description: Input and output tokens as the API counts them, at the API's boundary. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears already at 1, so a rate never sees that first event, and a series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.

defaults.noValue: Missing: no completion has been counted since the API process started, or no API target is scraped.

panels.title: Tokens per second at the API, by model and direction

panels.description: The runtime's own counters, mapped by the chart's recording rules. A different measurement from the API's, and not expected to match it.

defaults.noValue: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.
